questions.scenario: Your family is glued to the TV watching the ISRO Chandrayaan landing live. What is going through your mind?

options.text: Staring intensely at the screen, trying to visually identify the actual craters on the moon as the lander touches down.
Watching the telemetry graphs and speed numbers closely, mentally calculating if the velocity is dropping at the correct rate.
Recording the TV screen and your family's proud reaction to make an emotional WhatsApp status or Instagram Reel.
Explaining to your younger sibling how the ISRO chief is managing the massive team of tense scientists in the control room.

questions.scenario: It's a hot summer night, the power goes out ('light chali gayi'), and everyone goes to the terrace. What do you do?

options.text: Immediately grab your binoculars or just stare up, physically trying to connect the dots and spot famous constellations.
Use a sky map app to figure out exactly what time the International Space Station (ISS) will orbit over your city.
Balance your phone on the terrace wall and use the 'Pro' mode to try and capture a stunning long-exposure shot of the stars.
Make sure everyone has mosquito repellent, bring up the chairs, and organize a fun storytelling session in the dark.

questions.scenario: Your school takes you on a field trip to the Nehru Planetarium. Where are you focusing the most?

options.text: Trying to sneak to the front to see how that massive, mechanical star-projector in the center of the room actually works.
Listening closely to the guide explain the physics of black holes and asking a complex doubt about gravity.
Buying a cool, glow-in-the-dark solar system poster from the souvenir shop to decorate your bedroom wall.
Keeping your hyperactive friend group in check and organized so you don't get scolded by the strict class teacher.

questions.scenario: Your group has to make a Solar System model for the Science Exhibition. What is your role?

options.text: Physically cutting the thermocol balls, hammering the stand, and doing the messy, hands-on assembly yourself.
Calculating the exact mathematical scale ratio so that Jupiter is proportionally the correct size compared to Earth.
Painting the planets with beautiful, realistic textures and making sure the final presentation looks highly aesthetic.
Dividing the tasks among the group and managing the Rs. 300 budget collected for chart paper and glue.

questions.scenario: You are watching a great sci-fi movie with spaceships and time travel. What catches your attention?

options.text: Being totally fascinated by the realistic space suits, heavy rover vehicles, and the physical alien terrains.
Pausing the movie to analyze if the physics of time dilation and wormholes actually makes logical sense.
Admiring the stunning VFX, the background music, and how beautifully the galaxies and nebulas are shown.
Wondering how the movie director managed such a massive budget, huge sets, and a giant crew to make this happen.

questions.scenario: A rare Solar Eclipse is happening during school hours. How do you handle the excitement?

options.text: Finding the exact safe spot on the school ground and practically setting up a pinhole camera to view it safely.
Explaining the exact orbital mechanics to your friends about why the moon is perfectly blocking the sun today.
Taking an awesome, creative photo of the eclipse shadows forming through the tree leaves to post online.
Requesting the principal to officially delay the morning assembly so the entire school gets a chance to experience it.

questions.scenario: You find an old, dusty telescope locked away in your school's physics lab. What is your first instinct?

options.text: Spending your entire lunch break cleaning the lenses, tightening the heavy screws, and physically calibrating it.
Trying to figure out the mathematical formula of its optical power based on the curve of the glass lens.
Thinking about how 'vintage' and cool it looks, making it the perfect prop for a dark-academia photoshoot.
Pitching a solid idea to the science teacher to start an official 'Astronomy Club' using this found equipment.

questions.scenario: You are reading a newspaper article about ISRO planning a new mission to Mars. What interests you?

options.text: Reading about the actual hardware—the giant antennas and rovers they are building to survive the red dust.
Looking at the numbers—the speed required to escape Earth's gravity and the exact trajectory to reach Mars.
Looking at the artist's digital impression of the shiny rocket flying through space printed on the front page.
Reading about how the Indian government approved the massive budget and which scientists are leading the charge.

questions.scenario: You are at a local market buying a pair of binoculars for a family trip to the mountains. How do you pick one?

options.text: Testing the focus wheels, checking the grip, and loving the heavy, physical feel of the equipment in your hands.
Reading the box closely to understand the exact magnification ratio and focal length specifications before deciding.
Taking cool pictures *through* the binoculars with your phone camera to get that awesome circular-framed shot.
Negotiating a great discount with the shopkeeper and convincing your cousin to buy one too so you can share.

questions.scenario: Discussing the possibility of aliens with your cousins at a family wedding function. What's your take?

options.text: Arguing that we just need to build massive, stronger radio telescopes on ground to finally hear their signals.
Using mathematical probability logic to prove that in a universe this big, they absolutely must exist somewhere.
Talking about how cool it would be to design their alien spaceships and imagining what their cities look like.
Joking about how the UN should organize a diplomatic space mission to go negotiate a peace treaty with them.

Telescope_Operator.title: The Sky Scout (Observational Astronomer / Equipment Expert)
Telescope_Operator.primary_match_text: You are hands-on, practical, and love physical exploration. You don't just want to read about space in a book; you want to look through the lens, operate the heavy machinery, and see the universe with your own eyes.
Telescope_Operator.day_in_the_life: Working in high-altitude observatories (like Hanle in Ladakh), calibrating massive telescopes, staring into the deep night sky, and logging physical observations of stars and comets.
Telescope_Operator.alternative_match_text: If not astronomy, your love for physical instruments and the outdoors would make you a great Geologist, Mechanical Engineer, or Surveyor.
Telescope_Operator.roadmap: 11th/12th: Science (PCM is mandatory). Entrance: Crack JEE Main/Advanced or university entrances. Degree: B.Sc in Physics/Astronomy or B.Tech. Next Steps: Pursue an M.Sc and get hands-on internship experience at observatories like IUCAA or IIA.

Astrophysicist.title: The Cosmic Calculator (Astrophysicist / Orbital Analyst)
Astrophysicist.primary_match_text: You have a highly analytical and logical brain. You love physics, complex math, and uncovering the hidden laws of the universe. To you, space is a giant, beautiful puzzle waiting to be solved with numbers.
Astrophysicist.day_in_the_life: Sitting with supercomputers, analyzing complex ISRO data, calculating the gravity of black holes, and predicting the exact orbital path a satellite needs to take to reach Mars.
Astrophysicist.alternative_match_text: Your extreme logic and love for complex calculations make you a perfect fit for a Data Scientist, Quantum Physicist, or Aerospace Engineer.
Astrophysicist.roadmap: 11th/12th: Science (PCM is mandatory). Entrance: Crack JEE Advanced for IITs or IIST (Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology). Degree: B.Tech in Engineering Physics/Aerospace or B.Sc Physics. Next Steps: A Master's and PhD are usually required for top research roles.

Astrophotographer.title: The Universe Artist (Science Communicator / Astrophotographer)
Astrophotographer.primary_match_text: You are highly creative, visual, and have an eye for beauty. You want to take the complex, mysterious universe and translate it into stunning visuals, videos, and stories that everyone can understand and admire.
Astrophotographer.day_in_the_life: Traveling to dark-sky reserves to take long-exposure photos of the Milky Way, editing stunning space documentaries, running a popular science YouTube channel, and making space look magical.
Astrophotographer.alternative_match_text: With your amazing visual creativity, you would also excel as a Wildlife Photographer, VFX Artist, or Digital Marketing Creator.
Astrophotographer.roadmap: 11th/12th: Any stream (Science preferred for basic knowledge). Degree: B.Sc Physics, Bachelor of Design (B.Des), or Mass Communication. Next Steps: Build a massive digital portfolio, master camera equipment, and learn heavy editing software.

Mission_Director.title: The Space Commander (Space Mission Director / ISRO Manager)
Mission_Director.primary_match_text: You are a natural leader, organized, and a big-picture thinker. You know how to manage people, handle high-pressure situations, and coordinate massive projects. You are the captain of the ship.
Mission_Director.day_in_the_life: Sitting in the ISRO Mission Control center, managing a team of hundreds of scientists, handling the multi-crore budget, and giving the final 'Go/No-Go' command for a rocket launch.
Mission_Director.alternative_match_text: Your fantastic leadership and management skills would make you an incredible Corporate CEO, IAS Officer, or Airline Operations Manager.
Mission_Director.roadmap: 11th/12th: Science (PCM is mandatory). Entrance: Crack JEE Advanced for IIST or top NITs/IITs. Degree: B.Tech in Aerospace, Electronics, or Mechanical Engineering. Next Steps: Join ISRO as a Scientist/Engineer (via ICRB exams) and rise through the ranks via years of successful project management.
